g.text: 3-axis TMC2209 motion motherboard · 12-24 V in · 4-layer PCB
1. TMC2209 VS sits directly on VMOTOR. There is no ideal-diode
controller and no switched motor rail: motor current is cut at
the driver through ENN, which is what every RAMPS-class board
does. D1 alone handles surge and reverse polarity - it opens
F1 - so feed this board 12-24 V and nothing else.
2. J3 is a 2-pole NC e-stop. Pole A drives ESTOP_SENSE (GPIO15) so
firmware can stop the planner; pole B sits in series with Q1's
source, so ENN can only be pulled low when DRV_EN is high AND
the button is closed. That part is copper, not firmware.
3. Six endstops land on GPIO38-41 + GPIO13/14, straight onto the
MCU with no I²C expander anywhere in the path.
4. One analogue input: J17 → GPIO3 (ADC1_CH2). VMOTOR is
monitored on GPIO1 (ADC1_CH0) by the on-chip 12-bit ADC.
5. Three axes (U5-U7, J8-J10) and two outputs: discrete AO3400A
low-side switches, OUT1 5 V on J18, OUT2 24 V on J19.
6. A series SS36 drops the WS2812 strip VDD by one diode drop.
That helps 3.3 V data but is no guaranteed level shift: fit a
3.3 V-compatible strip or an external AHCT buffer.
7. GPIO35/36/37 are the N16R8 octal PSRAM and GPIO33/34 are not
bonded on WROOM-1; none are used. GPIO45/46 are the only spares.
8. VREF must be defined at reset because I_scale_analog resets
to 1: a 33 k / 10 k divider off 5VOUT gives a safe ~0.82 A_RMS
default until firmware clears the bit.
U5-U7 TMC2209 VS · OUT2 24 V via Q3
USB fallback → mux VIN2, only below 4.03 V on PR1
Q2 / OUT1 · WS2812 strip through D6 · U3 LDO input
ESP32-S3 · 3× VCC_IO · endstops + J17 · OLED · J21
TMC2209 channel, UART bus, ENN chain, DIAG pull-downs
6 direct-GPIO endstops, J17 analogue in, headers
Q2/Q3 low-side, RGB, LEDs, J21, test points
• 4 layers: L1 signal + components, L2 solid GND, L3 power planes (VMOTOR / 5V / 3V3 — there is no switched rail), L4 signal + GND fill.
• Every TMC2209 exposed pad soldered to GND with ≥ 16 thermal vias (0.3 mm drill / 0.6 mm pad) into L2 and L4. C_VS ceramics, the 22 nF charge-pump cap and the two 0.11 Ω sense
resistors all placed within 3 mm of their pins.
• LMR33630: copy the TI layout — C_IN on the same side, VIN/PGND loop < 4 mm², SW node kept small, no cut in the L2 pour underneath.
• ESP32-S3 antenna hangs over the board edge; keepout of ≥ 15 mm with no copper on any layer, no traces, no ground.
• USB D+/D- routed as a 90 Ω differential pair, < 40 mm, no vias, referenced to L2, with D5 USBLC6 within 5 mm of J4.
• Motor traces ≥ 1.5 mm on 1 oz copper, kept off L2, routed as tight A+/A- and B+/B- pairs to the connector.
• The two surviving analogue nodes are the VMOTOR divider (sheet 2) and J17's RC (sheet 8). Keep both ≥ 20 mm from the SW node and the motor
traces, and return them to L2 close to the module rather than out among the drivers.
• The e-stop is NOT a certified safety function. Pole B breaks Q1's source return in copper, so ENN releases all three drivers with no firmware in the
path — but VMOTOR and the 24 V output on J19 stay live. A load that must drop mechanically needs a third pole or an external contactor.
• Do not fit the 24 V flyback D3 below 60 V, and keep its loop to Q3 short: the AO3400A is only a 30 V part.
12-24 V in → VMOTOR · fuse + TVS · 2-pole e-stop
J1 and J2 are wired in parallel — fit whichever suits the machine.
J1 is a 3.5 A part, so use J2 above that, and when all three motors
24 V → 2.18 V and 30 V → 2.73 V, both inside the ESP32-S3 ADC1 range at
11 dB attenuation. Firmware only needs "is bulk present, and roughly what", so
the on-chip 12-bit ADC is all this needs.
E-STOP — 2-pole NC button: one pole to firmware, one in the ENN return
closed → low = running · pressed or cable cut → high = stopped
Pole B is wired in series with the source of Q1, the FET that pulls the shared
TMC2209 ENN line low (sheet 5). Opening the button breaks that return, ENN
floats up to +3V3 through R15, and all three drivers release their outputs.
That happens in copper, with no firmware in the path.
Pole A only tells firmware what happened, so it can stop the planner, drop the
step queue and forget its position instead of resuming into a moved axis.
This is NOT a certified safety function.
TRADE: the motor rail now stays live when stopped, so the 24 V output does not
de-energise mechanically. If a solenoid or brake must drop on e-stop, use a
3-pole button and put the third pole in that load, or an external contactor.
If no button is fitted, link A1-A2 and B1-B2. Without the B link the drivers
D1 and F1 are the whole input-protection scheme. There is no ideal-diode
controller, no overvoltage cut and no switched motor rail.
Reverse polarity — D1 is unidirectional, so a backwards input forward-biases
it and it blows F1. F1 is a replaceable cartridge in an OMNI-BLOK holder, so
the cost of a wrong-polarity plug is one fuse rather than one board.
Overvoltage — a 36 V or 48 V supply also drives D1 hard and opens F1, but the
drivers see the clamp voltage until it does. That is slow and not certain.
Switched rail — there is no VM_SW. Motor current is cut at the driver via ENN,
which is what every RAMPS-class board does. It also means a TMC2209 answers
over UART at boot, so the startup driver survey is a single pass.
3 · 5 V Buck, Priority Mux & 3.3 V LDO
3 · 5 V Buck, Priority Mux & 3.3 V LDO
5 V / 3 A STEP-DOWN — TI recommended configuration for 400 kHz, V_OUT = 5 V
Tapped straight off VMOTOR, downstream of F1 and D1 on sheet 2. There is no separate buck fuse or TVS.
D4 lights when PG is LOW = "5 V rail bad".
It runs off 5V_BUCK, so a dead buck leaves it dark.
EP is both AGND and the heatsink — solder it to the
L2 ground plane with ≥ 9 thermal vias.
5 V PRIORITY MUX — buck wins, USB is the fallback
MODE tied to VIN1 = automatic priority mode
PR1 threshold: V_IN1 switches away when PR1 falls below V_REF = 1.0 V.
V_trip = 1.0 V × (100 k + 33 k) / 33 k = 4.03 V, so the board hands over to USB only after the buck has genuinely collapsed.
ST is open-drain and pulls LOW while VIN1 is NOT in use, i.e. "running on USB". TP15 exposes it; it is deliberately not
wired to a GPIO because the only spare pins are GPIO45/46, which are strapping pins - read VMON instead.
The mux is rated 2.5 A, below the buck's 3 A. Loads above ~2 A (big LED strips) must be fed from their own connector,
SOT-223 tab is VOUT, NOT ground — the cooling pour is a 3V3 pour.
C22 is deliberately tantalum: the AMS1117 loop needs some ESR and can
oscillate on a pure MLCC output. Fit 22 µF/10 V tantalum or an MLCC with 0.5-1 Ω
Worst case: (5 − 3.3) × 0.5 A = 0.85 W. Give the tab ≥ 300 mm² of copper.
native USB · strapping pins respected · octal PSRAM pins avoided
Place C26/C27 within 3 mm of module pin 2.
EN network: 10 k pull-up + 10 µF (same 10 µF used everywhere on 3V3/5 V).
Gives ~100 ms of POR delay after 3V3 is valid.
GPIO0 is only a strap at reset. There is no runtime
user button: SW1 resets and SW2 straps for download.
USB-C 2.0 — data + conservative 500 mA, ESD protected
SHLD → GND through JP1. Replace with 1 MΩ ∥ 4.7 nF if the shield must float.
USB-only operation has a 500 mA total design budget. F2 is thermal protection, not a precision limiter.
The console can also run over native USB (USB-Serial-JTAG), so J5 is optional.
ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 PIN RULES — verified against the Espressif module datasheet
• GPIO35/36/37 (module pins 28-30) are wired to the in-package OCTAL PSRAM on any R8 part and are left unconnected here. GPIO33/34 are not bonded out at all.
• Strapping pins left floating so the module's internal weak pulls decide: GPIO45 (VDD_SPI = 3.3 V, weak pull-down) and GPIO46 (ROM print + boot, weak pull-down) are the
only two spare pins on the board and are deliberately left unconnected — do not hang a driven signal on either. GPIO0 has the only external strap: 10 k pull-up + SW2,
• GPIO3 is a strapping pin too (JTAG source select), but here it only sees J17's 1 k / 100 nF RC (sheet 8), so it still floats at reset. JTAG source select affects
neither boot mode nor flash voltage, so using GPIO3 as ADC1_CH2 is safe.
• GPIO19/20 carry native USB D-/D+ and nothing else; the PHY is internal so no series resistors are needed. GPIO43/44 stay on the U0 debug console.
• GPIO39-42 are also the external-JTAG pads (MTCK/MTDO/MTDI/MTMS). 39/40/41 are endstop inputs and 42 is OUT1_EN, which disables external JTAG
• GPIO39 idles HIGH after reset and GPIO21/42/47 fall more slowly than the rest. Each endstop has its own 10 k pull-up to 3V3 (sheet 8), each output gate a
10 k pull-down (sheet 9) and each DIAG input a 100 k pull-down (sheet 5), so nothing is left to the pin's own reset behaviour. DRV_EN on GPIO21 is the exception — see sheet 5.
• ANTENNA: the module must overhang the PCB edge. Keepout of ≥ 15 mm with no copper, no traces and no ground on any of the four layers, and no metal (motors,
heatsinks, connectors, chassis) within that volume. The buck inductor L1 and all three TMC2209 sit on the far side of the board (sheet 1 zoning).
5 · Axis M0 · TMC2209 Reference Channel, UART Bus & Enable Chain
TMC2209-LA-T standard application circuit · 0.11 Ω sense · UART address 0
5 · Axis M0 · TMC2209 Reference Channel, UART Bus & Enable Chain
AXIS M0 / X — U5 TMC2209-LA-T, complete channel per datasheet §3.1 · UART address 0
VS bank — low-ESR, ≤ 3 mm from pins 22/28, return straight into the EP thermal pad
SINGLE-WIRE UART BUS — shared by U5-U7 (datasheet fig. 4.1)
R13 is the only series element the datasheet asks for; RXD taps the bus
directly. R14 keeps the idle level HIGH so no driver sees a framing error
before the ESP32 UART is initialised. Set GCONF.pdn_disable = 1 in firmware
or standstill current reduction fights the bus.
DRIVER ENABLE — hardware AND of firmware and e-stop
Q1's source is ENN_RTN, not GND: e-stop pole B on J3 (sheet 2) closes
that return in copper. ENN can therefore only be pulled low when DRV_EN
is high AND the button is closed — a hardware AND with no firmware in
the path. ENN HIGH = all three power stages floating, and R15 holds it
there, so the board wakes up with the motors disabled.
The e-stop return is the only condition ANDed with DRV_EN. One FET, one
series contact, nothing else in the enable path.
R53 is mandatory: it holds Q1 V_GS at zero while GPIO21 is high-impedance
during reset, boot and with an unprogrammed MCU. Connect it gate-to-source
rather than gate-to-board-GND because Q1's source is the switched ENN_RTN.
DIAG PULL-DOWNS — fitted even with a driver left off
DIAG is push-pull, so these only hold an empty driver site's GPIO low.
CURRENT SETTING · VERIFIED AGAINST THE TMC2209 DATASHEET
I_RMS = 325 mV / (R_SENSE + 20 mΩ) × 1/√2 × V_VREF / 2.5 V. Fit 0.11 Ω, 2512, 1 W shunts and cap configured continuous current at 1.4 A_RMS per axis.
GCONF.i_scale_analog resets to 1, so VREF is live at power-up: the 33 k / 10 k divider takes 5VOUT down to 1.16 V → 0.82 A_RMS default. Firmware then clears the bit and sets IRUN/IHOLD over UART.
Do not load 5VOUT beyond the 25 mA the regulator allows; the divider draws 104 µA. The 4.7 µF ceramic must sit directly between pin 8 and the EP pad.
The 22 nF/50 V charge-pump capacitor sits between CPO and CPI and the 100 nF/50 V between VCP and VS — both are mandatory, both must be ≤ 3 mm from the package.
SPREAD, CLK and STDBY are tied to GND: internal 12 MHz clock, StealthChop as the reset default (UART can still flip it via GCONF.en_spreadCycle), standby disabled.
6 · Axis M1 · TMC2209 Channel & Per-Channel BOM
identical to M0 · UART address 1 · MS1_AD0 strapped high
6 · Axis M1 · TMC2209 Channel & Per-Channel BOM
AXIS M1 / Y — U6 TMC2209-LA-T, complete channel per datasheet §3.1 · UART address 1
VS bank — low-ESR, ≤ 3 mm from pins 22/28, return straight into the EP thermal pad
PER-CHANNEL COMPONENTS — THE SAME CIRCUIT THREE TIMES
Datasheet dissipation: 1.4 W at 1.0 A_RMS and 2.8 W at
1.4 A_RMS (24 V, two-phase sinewave, 20-40 kHz chopper).
R_th(j-a) = 30 K/W on a 2s2p multilayer board, R_th(j-c) = 6 K/W.
1.4 W → ΔT ≈ 42 K, so 1.0 A_RMS per axis is safe with a solid
plane; three axes together put 4.2 W into the same copper.
MOSFET R_DS(on) = 0.17 Ω typ / 0.21 Ω max per switch.
Continuous rating is 1.4 A_RMS/axis only after thermal validation in the final enclosure.
Rules: ≥ 16 vias (0.3 mm) per EP pad, ≥ 400 mm² of L2 copper
per driver, ≥ 15 mm between EP pads, no other heat source in
that band, and set the OTP/UART prewarning to 120 °C so
firmware can drop IRUN before the 150 °C shutdown.
WHY EVERY AXIS GETS ITS OWN PAGE
The three channels are electrically identical, so they are drawn as three full instances rather than one instance plus a note: it makes the netlist, the BOM line quantities
and the placement review unambiguous. Sheets 5-7 differ only in the reference designators, in the STEP/DIR/DIAG nets that reach the ESP32, and in the two address straps.

M1 is the Y axis on the chessboard, the zen garden and the line-art machine. On a 2-axis machine leave U7 and its passives off the board: nothing else depends on them, and R64 (sheet 5) keeps the empty DIAG input low.
7 · Axis M2 · TMC2209 Channel & Motor Interface Notes
identical to M0 · UART address 2 · MS2_AD1 strapped high
7 · Axis M2 · TMC2209 Channel & Motor Interface Notes
AXIS M2 / Z — U7 TMC2209-LA-T, complete channel per datasheet §3.1 · UART address 2
VS bank — low-ESR, ≤ 3 mm from pins 22/28, return straight into the EP thermal pad
Pinout is A+ A- B+ B- (coil A on pins 1-2, coil B on 3-4).
A NEMA17 with a 4-wire loom: measure the coils before wiring,
a swapped pair inside one coil only reverses that axis, but a
cross-coil swap (A+/B+) makes the motor buzz and stall.
Never unplug a motor while VMOTOR is live — and it is live
whenever the board is powered, e-stop or not. The
inductive kick can exceed the 32 V absolute maximum on VS.
Power the board down first; pressing the e-stop is not enough.
Traces ≥ 1.5 mm on 1 oz copper for 1.5 A_RMS, coil pairs
routed side by side so the chopper current loop stays small,
and kept off L2 so the return current does not cut the plane.
DIAG goes HIGH on overtemperature, short, undervoltage or a
StallGuard stall. Driver protection flags require ENN inactive;
the velocity-qualified StallGuard indication is not latched.
Each axis has its own DIAG pin on the ESP32 (GPIO10/11/12), so
firmware can tell which driver faulted; the shared DRV_ENN
then clears all three at once.
In UART mode MS1/MS2 are the address, NOT the microstep
selector: resolution comes from CHOPCONF.MRES (1 to 1/256
with interpolation), so the straps never need to change when
StallGuard4 needs StealthChop; sensorless homing therefore
works on this board without any endstop on that axis.
AXIS ASSIGNMENT PER PROJECT · AND WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ON THIS BOARD
Chessboard: M0 = X gantry, M1 = Y gantry, M2 unused; the electromagnet hangs on OUT2, the 24 V low-side switch on sheet 9.
Zen garden: M0 = radial arm, M1 = turntable, M2 = optional tool lift; the LED strip runs from the RGB header J20.
Line-art machine: M0 = X, M1 = Y, M2 = pen lift; the string-tension sensor lands on J17 → GPIO3 (ADC1_CH2) and the six endstops go straight to GPIO (sheet 8).
No motor-current sense amplifier: the TMC2209 regulates coil current itself and reports through DIAG/StallGuard, so an external shunt would add heat and noise for no gain.
No opto-isolation on STEP/DIR: everything shares one ground and the drivers are on the same PCB, which is what makes the 0.11 Ω sense resistors and short VS loops possible.
No per-axis fuse: F1 protects the whole 12-24 V input and the drivers current-limit themselves. A shorted motor cable trips the driver's short detection into DIAG, not the fuse.
6 direct-GPIO endstops · one ADC1 input · 400 kHz bus for OLED / expansion
ENDSTOP INPUTS — 6 × filtered, pulled up, no clamp diodes, straight onto GPIO
Either a dry contact from SIG to GND, or a 3.3 V open-drain hall sensor fed from pin 1. Both idle high and pull low, so firmware selects the type
per input. 1 k + 100 nF = 100 µs assert, 10 k gives 1 ms release. The 1 k : 10 k divider adds 0.30 V, so sensor V_OL must stay under 0.55 V to
clear the ESP32-S3's 0.825 V V_IL. No clamp diodes: the 1 k and 100 nF are the only protection. Never feed 5 V, 24 V or PNP into SIG.
The board has one analogue input. GPIO3 is ADC1_CH2, so it
can be read while WiFi is up — ADC2 cannot. 1 k + 100 nF gives
~100 µs settling, which is plenty for a tension or pot reading.
No clamp diode here either — R52 and C61 are the protection.
A load cell needs its own amplifier (HX711 or INA125) on the
sensor; use 0-2.9 V for calibrated measurement. Never exceed 3.3 V or feed 5 V / 24 V.
Pin 1 of J11-J16 only. A pinched sensor cable trips F3 instead of
browning out the ESP32. Plain switches ignore this branch entirely.
F3 holds 0.1 A, so six 3.6 mA hall sensors leave 4× margin.
WHAT THIS SHEET COSTS IN GPIO
WHY ENDSTOPS GO STRAIGHT TO THE MCU
All six endstops sit on real GPIOs with real edge interrupts
rather than behind an I²C expander, so an assert is visible to
firmware immediately instead of costing a bus round trip behind
an interrupt pin. That is worth the pins it spends: GPIO38-41
plus GPIO13/14 carry them, and the table above is the bill.
The same argument covers the analogue side. One input on GPIO3
(ADC1_CH2) and VMOTOR sensing on GPIO1 (ADC1_CH0) both use the
on-chip 12-bit ADC, so there is no external ADC and nothing on
the I²C bus that the board itself depends on.
I²C ADDRESS MAP AND BUS BUDGET
Nothing on the board sits on the bus. R38/R39 (4.7 k) pull it
up for whatever is plugged into J6 or J7.
0x3C or 0x3D: typical SSD1306 OLED on J6. Everything else free.
400 kHz is the design speed; with only header capacitance
(~60 pF) the ESP32 can run the bus faster if you want to.
J7 is a 4-pin header with no INT pin: there is no spare
interrupt-capable GPIO to give it, because GPIO45/46 are
strapping pins and must stay undriven.
I²C BUS · PULL-UPS · OLED HEADER · EXPANSION HEADER
One 4.7 k pair serves the whole bus — just the OLED header and the expansion header (~60 pF total).
ENDSTOPS — MECHANICAL SWITCH OR HALL SENSOR, SELECTED IN FIRMWARE
Switch: dry contact between pin 3 (SIG) and pin 2 (GND); pin 1 unused. Hall: 3.3 V open-drain, VCC on pin 1, OUT on pin 3.
DRV5033 (2.5-38 V, 22 Ω r_DS(on), 13 µs) is the reference part; its TO-92 suits frame mounting.
Do not fit a duty-cycled sensor such as the DRV5032, whose open-drain versions sample at 20 Hz and can take 75 ms to report.
Allegro A110x needs 3.8 V and will not run here. Decouple each sensor at the sensor with 100 nF.
A hall sensor that loses power reads as released, unlike an NC contact: configure the axis inverted in firmware if you want a
GPIO CHOICE FOR THE SIX ENDSTOPS
GPIO38-41 are the old SPI block, freed by deleting the microSD socket and the SPI expansion header. GPIO13/14 came free with the
dropped fourth axis. All six are plain input-capable pins on ADC2 or on no ADC at all, so nothing here fights WiFi.
GPIO39 idles HIGH after reset, which is the released state for these inputs, so a reset never looks like a triggered endstop.
None of the six is a strapping pin, so an endstop held closed at power-up cannot change boot mode or flash voltage. That is why
GPIO45/46 stayed empty instead of taking two of these inputs.
Each input has its own 10 k pull-up to 3V3. Firmware also enables the internal pull-up, which only adds a weak parallel path.
WHAT THE ON-CHIP ADC IS GOOD FOR
12 bits over an approximately 0-2.9 V calibrated range at 11 dB attenuation, and the ESP32-S3 SAR ADC is noisier and less linear than a dedicated part.
That is acceptable here because both measurements are coarse: "is the motor supply present, and roughly what" on GPIO1,
and a slow tension or position reading on GPIO3. Average in firmware and apply the calibration curve from efuse.
If a project genuinely needs 16-bit resolution, put an ADS1115 on J7 as a daughterboard - the bus and the 3V3 pin are there for it.
9 · Power Outputs, RGB, LEDs & Test Points
2 discrete low-side FET outputs · WS2812 · rail LEDs · aux power · probe points
9 · Power Outputs, RGB, LEDs & Test Points
OUT1 — 5 V LOW-SIDE SWITCH · Q2 AO3400A · gate from GPIO42
OUT1 · PWM · fan, 5 V solenoid, lamp
R54 damps the gate edge, R55 holds the gate at 0 V on an unprogrammed or reset board — that
pull-down is the only thing keeping the output off before firmware runs, so do not omit it.
5V_SYS sits behind the 2.5 A TPS2116 (sheet 3), so the AO3400A is the limit here: budget 1 A.
The load's + lead goes to J18 pin 1 and Q2 breaks the return on pin 2. D2 is mandatory.
OUT2 — 12-24 V LOW-SIDE SWITCH · Q3 AO3400A · gate from GPIO2
Fed from VMOTOR, which is live whenever the board is powered. Pressing the e-stop cuts motor
torque at ENN but does NOT de-energise this output. A solenoid or brake that must drop
mechanically needs a 3-pole e-stop button or an external contactor — see sheet 2.
AO3400A is a 30 V part on a 24 V rail: keep D3's loop short and never feed more than 24 V in.
ADDRESSABLE RGB OUTPUT — GPIO48 direct, strip VDD dropped by D6
No level shifter. D6 lowers strip VDD by one Schottky drop, but its drop depends on strip current.
Use a current WS2812B V6 strip specified for 3.3 V data. Older 0.7 × VDD variants have no
guaranteed worst-case margin here; add an external AHCT buffer if the fitted strip requires 5 V logic.
D6 is supply isolation, not a substitute for checking the exact pixel datasheet.
R58 damps the line reflection and must stay at the driver end, not at the strip. C62 is the head-of-strip
reservoir the WS2812 datasheet asks for. RGB_DATA is GPIO48, so the 800 kHz waveform comes out of the
RMT peripheral in hardware and is immune to WiFi jitter.
Three always-on rail indicators, and they double as a first-look diagnostic: VMOTOR lit but
5 V dark isolates the buck, 5 V lit but 3V3 dark isolates the LDO.
R59 is the same 10 k as the rest of the board: 2.1 mA at 24 V, 45 mW in a 0603.
There is no discrete STATUS or ERROR LED. Firmware state is the first pixel on J20.
J21 feeds daughterboards — the chess Hall-sensor matrix, an
external driver, a servo rail. VMOTOR is limited only by F1, so
fuse the daughterboard itself. Budget ~150 mA on 5V_SYS, 300 mA on 3V3.
TEST POINTS — 1 mm pads, probe-loop friendly
TP1 VMOTOR (sheet 2), TP2 5V_BUCK and TP15 (TPS2116 ST) on sheet 3 are drawn next to the
nodes they belong to. TP1-TP4 are the rail-by-rail power check: probe
them in order before fitting U4 or any TMC2209.
TP5/TP6 sit at opposite corners for a scope ground spring; TP7/TP8 are pad-only.
• Both channels are discrete low-side N-FETs: the load's positive lead goes to the
connector's +V pin and the FET breaks the return. Do not swap the pins.
• Each gate has a 1 k series resistor and a 10 k pull-down. The pull-down is what
leaves the output off on an unprogrammed, reset or disconnected MCU. Keep it.
• Flyback diodes are mandatory for solenoids, relays, valves, pumps and electro-
magnets. D2 and D3 are both SS36 (60 V / 3 A).
• The AO3400A sets the limit on both channels: budget 1 A continuous, V_DS under
30 V. 5V_SYS is further capped by the 2.5 A mux, and by F2's 500 mA PTC on USB.
• Both gates are 3.3 V driven. AO3400A V_GS(th) is 1.45 V max and R_DS(on) is
31 mΩ at 4.5 V, so expect roughly 50 mΩ at 3.3 V — 50 mV of drop at 1 A.
WHY DISCRETE SWITCHES RATHER THAN AN ARRAY
Two AO3400A low-side switches, reusing the part number already on the board for
the driver-enable FET. A darlington array would bring a higher voltage rating and
internal clamps, but also a new part number and more board area than two SOT-23s.
The trade is that D2 and D3 are the only clamp on either channel, so an inductive
load with no flyback fitted will take the FET with it.
Status is the addressable pixel on J20 rather than discrete status and error LEDs,
which keeps the whole UI to one part and one GPIO.
1. No ICs fitted: check F1 and D1 orientation. Apply 12 V through a
current-limited supply and confirm VMOTOR at TP1.
2. Fit U1 and the buck passives. Confirm 5.0 V ± 2 % at TP2 with no load.
3. Fit U2 and U3. Confirm TP3 = 5.0 V and TP4 = 3.3 V, and check the 3V3 LED.
Then unplug the barrel jack and plug in USB: TP3 must hold 5 V and TP15
must pull LOW, which is the mux reporting it has handed over.
4. Fit U4. Confirm USB enumeration and flash a blink sketch. GPIO0 strap
check. Read VMON on GPIO1 and confirm it tracks the input.
5. Close J3 (or link A1-A2 and B1-B2). Confirm ESTOP_SENSE goes low.
6. Fit Q1. With the ESP32 held in reset, confirm DRV_ENN sits at 3V3, then
drive DRV_EN high and confirm DRV_ENN falls only while J3 is closed.
7. Fit U5 only. Read IFCNT over UART at address 0, then run one axis at 0.3 A.
8. Fit U6 and U7, then Q2/Q3 and the output stages last.
9. Cold-start F1 a dozen times from the real supply with everything fitted.
Inrush is about a third of the fast-acting I²t, so if it ever nuisance-trips,
drop the 6.3 A Slo-Blo 045406.3MR into the same holder.
GPIO45 and GPIO46 are the only unused pins, and both are strapping
pins: leave them unconnected rather than routing them to a header.
GPIO0 is the BOOT strap and GPIO19/20 and GPIO43/44 are USB and the
debug console. Everything else is allocated on sheets 4-9.
If a project needs more I/O, hang it off J7 (I²C) or J21 (power) as a
daughterboard. There is no room left on the module itself.
